categories.name: Agriculture & Livelihood
categories.blurb: Practical food-growing, fishing, and local trade skills shared by people who work with land and water.
intro: Agriculture and livelihood skills are best learned where they are used: in a garden, on a boat, at a market stall, or beside someone who has spent years doing the work. A skills exchange lets you learn those practical foundations from a community member instead of a generic course.

PalTuro connects learners with mentors who can teach farming, fishing, and local trades through conversation and hands-on practice. You bring curiosity and a skill to share; your mentor brings experience from their own livelihood.

faqs.q: What agriculture skills can I learn through a skills exchange?
faqs.a: Common starting points include vegetable gardening, soil preparation, planting schedules, fishing basics, and small local trades. The exact skills depend on the mentors in your community.

faqs.q: Do I need land or equipment to start?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many learners start with container gardening, a shared plot, or observation sessions. Ask your mentor what you need before the first meeting.

faqs.q: Is a skills exchange free?
faqs.a: PalTuro is free to join. The exchange is reciprocal: you teach something you know and learn something you want to learn.

skills.name: Farming
skills.summary: Learn the seasonal, soil, and planting basics of growing food from someone who farms.
learn: Watering, pest awareness, and harvest timing
prepare: A small plot, containers, or access to a community garden
A notebook for seasonal notes and questions
questions: What grows well in my area and season?
How do you decide when to harvest?

faqs.q: Can I learn farming if I only have a balcony?
faqs.a: Yes. Many mentors can teach container gardening, soil mixing, and small-space planting before you move to a larger plot.

faqs.q: How long does it take to learn the basics?
faqs.a: You can learn the core planting and care routine in a few sessions, but timing and observation matter. A full season gives you the most useful feedback.

skills.name: Fishing
skills.summary: Understand fishing basics, water reading, and responsible catch practices from experienced fishers.
learn: Reading weather, tides, and safe water conditions
prepare: Comfort with water and basic safety
A mentor-approved gear list before any trip
questions: What should I never do without a local guide?
Which seasons and conditions are safest for beginners?

faqs.q: Is fishing learned online?
faqs.a: The principles can be discussed online, but safety and technique should be learned with an experienced local mentor. Never fish alone as a beginner.

faqs.q: What safety rules matter most?
faqs.a: Check the weather, use appropriate gear, follow local regulations, and never go out without someone who knows the water.

skills.name: Local Trades
skills.summary: Learn practical neighborhood trades and small-business skills from people who run them.
learn: Basic tools and materials for a local trade
How to price and explain a simple service

A few questions about tools, costs, and safety
questions: What does a beginner need to buy first?

faqs.q: Can I learn a trade without quitting my job?
faqs.a: Yes. Many people start with weekend observation, small practice jobs, and a mentor who can review their work.

faqs.q: Do I need capital to start?
faqs.a: It depends on the trade. Ask your mentor what the minimum tool set is and what can be borrowed or practiced first.

categories.name: Cooking & Culinary
categories.blurb: Filipino cooking and dessert-making taught through family recipes, technique, and shared kitchen time.
intro: Filipino cooking is learned through repetition, taste, and the stories around the table. A skills exchange pairs you with a home cook or dessert maker who can explain the why behind the recipe, not just the ingredient list.
You can start with a single dish, a technique, or a family specialty. The goal is confidence in the kitchen and a real person you can ask when the recipe does not behave.

faqs.q: What Filipino cooking skills can I learn?
faqs.a: Learners often start with adobo, sinigang, pinakbet, kakanin, and basic knife and seasoning skills. The exact menu depends on your mentor.

faqs.q: Do I need a full kitchen?
faqs.a: No. Many sessions start with one pot, a few ingredients, and a mentor who can adapt the recipe to what you have.

faqs.q: Can I teach cooking if I am not a chef?
faqs.a: Yes. If you can cook a dish consistently and explain your process, you can teach it through a skills exchange.

skills.name: Filipino Cooking
skills.summary: Learn Filipino dishes and kitchen technique from a home cook who can explain the process.
learn: Building flavor with soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and aromatics
Balancing sour, salty, and sweet in Filipino dishes
Planning a family meal from one or two pots
prepare: A short list of dishes you want to learn
Basic ingredients for your first session
questions: How do you adjust a recipe for your family's taste?
Which steps can be prepared ahead?

faqs.q: Can I learn adobo through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Adobo is often one of the first dishes a cooking mentor teaches. It is a dish, not a separate skill page: it sits inside Filipino Cooking.

faqs.q: What if I do not have the exact ingredients?
faqs.a: Ask your mentor for substitutions before the session. Filipino cooking is flexible, and a good mentor will explain what can change.

skills.name: Filipino Dessert Making
skills.summary: Learn kakanin, cakes, and Filipino sweets with guidance on texture, timing, and local ingredients.
learn: Sweetness and texture adjustments for local ingredients
prepare: A dessert you want to make first
Basic measuring tools and a steamer or oven
questions: How do you know when a kakanin is set?
Which desserts travel well for sharing?

faqs.q: Do I need a steamer?
faqs.a: For many kakanin, yes. Ask your mentor whether a bamboo steamer, metal steamer, or oven adaptation is appropriate for the dessert you want to learn.

faqs.q: Can I learn dessert making for a small business?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask your mentor about batch sizes, shelf life, packaging, and costing after you learn the basic recipe.

categories.name: Household Skills
categories.blurb: Everyday home skills, from kitchen systems to decorating, taught by people who keep homes working.
intro: Household skills are easy to dismiss because they look ordinary, but they save time, money, and stress. A skills exchange lets you learn the routines and small techniques that make a home easier to run.
Whether you want a better kitchen workflow or a more comfortable room, a mentor can show you what they actually do and why it works.

faqs.q: What household skills can I learn?
faqs.a: Common requests include kitchen organization, meal prep routines, basic home decorating, and everyday repair and maintenance habits.

faqs.q: Is this only for people running a home?
faqs.a: No. Renters, students, and anyone who wants more control over their space can learn these skills.

faqs.q: Can household skills be taught online?
faqs.a: Many can. A mentor can walk through a room, a routine, or a problem on a video call and give you a plan to try.

skills.name: Home Decorating
skills.summary: Make a room feel intentional with layout, light, color, and budget-friendly choices.
prepare: Photos or measurements of the room
A budget range and one problem you want to solve
questions: What should I fix before buying anything?
How do I make a rental feel like mine?

faqs.q: Do I need to buy new furniture?
faqs.a: Usually not. A good first session focuses on rearranging what you already own before spending money.

faqs.q: Can you help with a rental unit?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask your mentor about removable fixes, wall-safe options, and changes your landlord will accept.

skills.name: Kitchen Basics
skills.summary: Build a kitchen routine around safe prep, simple tools, and meals you can repeat.
learn: Storage, cleaning, and food safety habits
prepare: A list of the meals you actually cook
A photo of your kitchen setup
questions: What tools are worth buying first?
How do I plan meals without wasting food?

faqs.q: Is this a cooking class?
faqs.a: It is broader. Kitchen Basics covers the routines, tools, and safety habits that make cooking easier, not just one recipe.

faqs.q: Can I learn with a small kitchen?
faqs.a: Yes. Small-kitchen organization and multi-use tools are common topics.

categories.name: Language & Writing
categories.blurb: Calligraphy and Philippine script writing taught through practice, history, and patient feedback.
intro: Writing is a physical skill as much as a mental one. A skills exchange gives you a person who can watch your hand, correct your form, and explain the history behind the letters.
You can learn calligraphy for personal projects or study Philippine scripts as a way to connect with language and heritage. Start with a script or style that interests you.

faqs.q: Can I learn Baybayin through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Baybayin is a topic inside Philippine Script Writing. A mentor can teach the script, writing practice, and the context around it.

faqs.q: Do I need special pens?
faqs.a: For calligraphy, a basic pen and paper are enough to start. Ask your mentor before buying a full set.

faqs.q: Is this only for artists?
faqs.a: No. These skills are for anyone who wants to write more clearly, learn a script, or understand the craft.

skills.name: Calligraphy
skills.summary: Learn letterforms, spacing, and pen control through guided practice.
prepare: A pen, paper, and a few reference words
A quiet surface and 20–30 minutes to practice
questions: Which script should a beginner start with?
How do I fix inconsistent spacing?

faqs.q: How often should I practice?
faqs.a: Short, regular practice beats long occasional sessions. Your mentor can give you a 15-minute drill routine.

faqs.q: Can I learn online?
faqs.a: Yes. A mentor can demonstrate strokes on camera and review photos of your work.

skills.name: Philippine Script Writing
skills.summary: Study Philippine scripts such as Baybayin through writing practice and historical context.
prepare: A notebook and a few words you want to write
Curiosity about the script's history

faqs.q: Is Baybayin a language?
faqs.a: No. Baybayin is a script. It can be used to write Philippine languages, and its history and usage are worth learning carefully.

faqs.q: Can I learn a Philippine script in a few sessions?
faqs.a: You can learn the basic characters and writing routine quickly, but reading and historical context take longer.

categories.name: Martial Arts
categories.blurb: Filipino martial arts taught with discipline, safety, and respect for the tradition.
intro: Filipino martial arts combine movement, timing, and respect for the people who keep the tradition alive. A skills exchange can connect you with a practitioner who teaches the foundations safely.
Start with stance, footwork, and control before speed. A good mentor will be clear about what is appropriate for your experience level.

faqs.q: Can I learn Arnis through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Arnis is a topic inside Filipino Martial Arts. A mentor can teach foundational movements, safety, and the history of the practice.

faqs.q: Do I need equipment?
faqs.a: Ask your mentor first. Some sessions start with empty-hand movement and borrowed practice tools.

faqs.q: Is this suitable for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes, with a mentor who teaches foundations and safety. Be honest about your experience and any physical limitations.

skills.name: Filipino Martial Arts
skills.summary: Learn foundational Filipino martial arts movement, safety, and discipline.
learn: Training safety and respect for the tradition
prepare: Comfortable clothing and water
A clear statement of your experience and limitations
questions: What should a beginner practice first?
How do I train safely at home?

faqs.q: What is the difference between Arnis, Eskrima, and Kali?
faqs.a: The terms overlap and are used differently across regions and schools. Ask your mentor how they use the terms and what their lineage teaches.

faqs.q: Can I learn without a sparring partner?
faqs.a: You can learn footwork and solo drills, but partner practice needs supervision. Do not spar without an experienced instructor.

categories.name: Modern Practical Skills
categories.blurb: Programming, design, sewing, motorcycle care, and other skills for work and daily life.
intro: Practical skills are the ones you can use immediately: a repair, a design, a small program, or a better way to care for the things you own. A skills exchange connects you with someone who does the work in real life.
You can start with a single project and build from there. The best mentors will help you understand the process, not just copy a finished result.

faqs.q: What practical skills can I learn?
faqs.a: Popular areas include programming, graphic design, sewing, motorcycle maintenance, nail art, T-shirt printing, woodworking, and roller skating.

faqs.q: Can I learn a practical skill without expensive tools?
faqs.a: Often yes. Ask your mentor what the minimum setup is and what you can borrow, rent, or practice without buying.

faqs.q: Can these skills lead to income?
faqs.a: Some can. Ask your mentor about the realistic path, costs, and practice time before treating a skill as a business.

skills.name: Flairtending
skills.summary: Learn bottle and tool handling, performance, and safe practice for flair bartending.
prepare: Practice bottles or a flair training set
A clear, uncluttered practice space
questions: What should I practice before touching glass?
How do I build a short routine?

faqs.q: Is flairtending dangerous?
faqs.a: It can be if you start with glass or try advanced moves too early. Begin with training tools and a mentor who teaches safety.

faqs.q: Do I need bartending experience?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but basic drink knowledge helps. Ask your mentor whether they teach flair alone or bartending plus flair.

skills.name: Graphic Design
skills.summary: Learn layout, type, color, and a repeatable design process for real projects.
prepare: A project you want to make
Access to a design tool or even paper
questions: What should I learn first: tools or design principles?
How do I get feedback on my work?

faqs.q: Do I need expensive software?
faqs.a: No. Start with a free tool or paper. Your mentor can help you choose software after you understand the principles.

faqs.q: Can I learn design without drawing well?
faqs.a: Yes. Graphic design is mostly about communication, layout, and decisions. Drawing is a separate skill.

skills.name: Motorcycle Maintenance
skills.summary: Learn the checks, tools, and maintenance habits that keep a motorcycle safe.
learn: Oil, chain, tire, and brake basics
When to fix it yourself and when to see a mechanic
prepare: Your motorcycle manual
A basic tool set and a safe workspace
questions: Which checks should I do every week?
What should I never attempt without a mechanic?

faqs.q: Can I learn maintenance on my own motorcycle?
faqs.a: Yes, with supervision. Start with checks and simple adjustments; leave safety-critical repairs to a qualified mechanic until you are trained.

faqs.q: What tools should a beginner buy?
faqs.a: Ask your mentor to review your manual and recommend a small set for your specific motorcycle.

skills.name: Nail Art
skills.summary: Learn nail preparation, color, and simple art techniques with a clean, safe setup.

A practice hand or a friend willing to model
questions: What should a beginner buy first?
How do I keep tools clean and safe?

faqs.q: Do I need a full professional kit?
faqs.a: No. Start with the essentials and add tools as your skills grow. Ask your mentor what they actually use.

faqs.q: Can I practice on myself?
faqs.a: Yes, but start with simple designs and follow hygiene guidance. Do not use damaged or shared tools without proper cleaning.

skills.name: Programming
skills.summary: Choose a programming path and learn the fundamentals through small, real projects.
intro: Programming is easier to learn when you have a person who can review your code and explain the next step. A skills exchange can connect you with a developer who teaches through small projects.
You do not need to learn everything at once. Start with one language or one project, then build the habit of reading errors, testing, and asking better questions.

faqs.q: Which programming language should I start with?
faqs.a: It depends on your goal. Python is common for beginners and data work; JavaScript/TypeScript is common for web development; C# is used in games and Windows applications.

faqs.q: Can I learn programming without a degree?
faqs.a: Yes. A mentor can help you build a project-based learning path, but consistency and practice matter more than the credential.

children.name: General Programming
children.summary: Learn programming fundamentals, problem solving, and a repeatable learning habit.
learn: Breaking a problem into small steps
prepare: A computer and a code editor
One small project idea
questions: How do I choose my first language?
How much math do I need?

faqs.q: Do I need to be good at math?
faqs.a: Most beginner programming needs basic logic more than advanced math. Specialized fields vary, so ask your mentor about your goal.

faqs.q: How do I practice between sessions?
faqs.a: Keep a small project and a list of errors. Bring the errors to your mentor instead of trying to hide them.

children.name: Python Programming
children.summary: Learn Python through scripts, data tasks, and small automations.
learn: Using libraries for a small project
prepare: Python installed on your computer
A small task you want to automate
questions: What should I build first?
How do I organize a growing script?

faqs.q: Is Python good for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes. Its readable syntax makes it a common first language, especially for automation, data, and scripting.

faqs.q: Can I learn Python online?
faqs.a: Yes. A mentor can review your code remotely and give you small exercises between sessions.

children.name: C# Programming
children.summary: Learn C# fundamentals and object-oriented thinking through small applications.

A small console or desktop project idea
questions: What is object-oriented programming?
Should I learn C# for game development?

faqs.q: Is C# only for Windows?
faqs.a: No. C# runs on multiple platforms, though some tools and frameworks are more common on Windows.

faqs.q: Can I learn C# as a first language?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have a mentor who can explain the structure and give you small projects.

children.name: Web Development
children.summary: Learn HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and the process of building a small website.
learn: A simple deploy and debugging workflow
prepare: A browser and code editor
A small site or page you want to build
questions: Should I learn a framework first?
How do I make a site accessible?

faqs.q: Do I need to learn design too?
faqs.a: Basic layout and accessibility help, but you can learn them alongside development. Ask your mentor how they split the work.

faqs.q: How do I practice web development?
faqs.a: Build small pages, inspect real sites, and ask for feedback on one page at a time.

skills.name: Roller Skating
skills.summary: Learn balance, stopping, and safe practice from a patient skater.
prepare: Skates and protective gear
A smooth, safe practice area
questions: What gear should a beginner wear?
How do I practice without falling badly?

faqs.q: Is roller skating hard to learn?
faqs.a: It takes practice, but most beginners can learn basic balance and stopping with guidance and protective gear.

faqs.q: Can I learn as an adult?
faqs.a: Yes. Many adults start from zero. Go at your own pace and prioritize safety.

skills.name: Sewing
skills.summary: Learn machine basics, seams, and simple repairs so you can make and mend clothes.
prepare: A sewing machine or access to one
Fabric, thread, and a simple project
questions: What should I make first?
How do I fix tension problems?

faqs.q: Do I need an expensive machine?
faqs.a: No. A basic machine that sews a straight stitch is enough to learn. Ask your mentor to help you test one before buying.

faqs.q: Can I learn sewing by hand?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand sewing is a useful foundation and enough for repairs and simple projects.

skills.name: T-Shirt Printing
skills.summary: Learn a simple printing workflow, from artwork to a wearable test print.
prepare: A design idea and a blank shirt
A workspace with ventilation
questions: Which printing method is best for a beginner?
How do I make a print last?

faqs.q: Can I print at home?
faqs.a: Some methods are home-friendly, but ventilation and safety matter. Ask your mentor which method fits your space.

faqs.q: Do I need a heat press?
faqs.a: Not for every method. Ask your mentor what the minimum setup is for the technique they teach.

skills.name: Woodworking
skills.summary: Learn safe hand-tool basics and build a simple, useful wooden project.
prepare: A simple project plan
Access to basic hand tools and a safe workspace
questions: Which tools should I buy first?
How do I work safely in a small space?

faqs.q: Can I start without power tools?
faqs.a: Yes. Hand tools are a good way to learn control and safety before adding power tools.

faqs.q: What is a good first project?
faqs.a: A simple box or shelf teaches measuring, cutting, assembly, and finishing without requiring advanced joinery.

categories.name: Performing Arts
categories.blurb: Folk dance, traditional music, and vocal music taught through practice and cultural context.
intro: Performing arts are learned by doing, watching, and repeating. A skills exchange gives you a mentor who can demonstrate the form, correct your timing, and explain the culture behind it.
You can start with a single song, dance, or instrument. The goal is confidence and respect for the tradition, not a perfect stage performance on day one.

faqs.q: Can I learn Tinikling through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Tinikling is a topic inside Folk Dance. A mentor can teach the steps, rhythm, and safety around the bamboo poles.

faqs.q: Do I need previous performance experience?
faqs.a: No. Many learners start as adults with no formal background.

faqs.q: Can I learn online?
faqs.a: Some foundations can be taught online, but dance and instruments often need in-person practice for timing and safety.

skills.name: Folk Dance
skills.summary: Learn Philippine folk dance steps, rhythm, and cultural context with a patient mentor.
prepare: Comfortable clothing and water
A clear space to practice
questions: What should I practice first?
How do I dance safely around props?

faqs.q: Is Tinikling hard for beginners?
faqs.a: The basic steps can be learned with guidance, but the bamboo timing takes practice. Start slowly and never practice advanced footwork without a mentor.

faqs.q: Can I learn folk dance as an adult?
faqs.a: Yes. Many community groups welcome adult beginners.

skills.name: Traditional Music
skills.summary: Learn traditional instruments, rhythm, and ensemble listening from a practitioner.
learn: Listening and playing in an ensemble
prepare: Access to the instrument or a practice alternative
A short rhythm or piece you want to learn
questions: Which instrument should I start with?
How do I practice without disturbing neighbors?

faqs.q: Do I need my own instrument?
faqs.a: Not always. Ask your mentor about practice instruments, shared spaces, or temporary alternatives.

faqs.q: Is traditional music only for advanced musicians?
faqs.a: No. Many traditions have beginner patterns and ensemble roles that can be learned step by step.

skills.name: Vocal Music
skills.summary: Learn breathing, pitch, and song interpretation, including Filipino vocal traditions.
prepare: A quiet practice space
A song you want to work on
questions: How do I practice without straining my voice?
How do I choose a song for my range?

faqs.q: Can I learn Kundiman through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Kundiman is a topic inside Vocal Music. A mentor can teach the style, phrasing, and vocal approach.

faqs.q: Do I need to read music?
faqs.a: Not to start. Many vocal mentors teach by ear and add notation as needed.

categories.name: Traditional Crafts
categories.blurb: Weaving, embroidery, costume making, and parol-making taught through hands-on practice.
intro: Traditional crafts carry memory and technique. A skills exchange lets you learn from someone who practices the craft, not just reads about it.
Start with a small piece and a technique you can repeat. Respect the tradition, credit your teacher, and practice before trying to sell or teach.

faqs.q: Can I learn Inabel weaving through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Inabel is a topic inside Philippine Handweaving. A mentor can teach loom basics, patterns, and the cultural context.

faqs.q: Do I need a loom?
faqs.a: For weaving, access to a loom matters. Ask your mentor about shared workspaces, small-frame alternatives, or practice methods.

faqs.q: Can I learn a craft online?
faqs.a: Some foundations and pattern reading can be taught online, but many crafts need in-person practice and materials.

skills.name: Costume Making
skills.summary: Learn measuring, construction, and finishing for performance and cultural costumes.
prepare: A costume reference or design
Basic sewing tools and fabric
questions: What should I make first?
How do I fit a costume without a dress form?

faqs.q: Do I need advanced sewing skills?
faqs.a: Start with simple constructions and repairs. Ask your mentor which project matches your current level.

faqs.q: Can I learn costume making without a sewing machine?
faqs.a: Some parts can be hand-sewn, but larger costumes usually need a machine. Ask your mentor what is realistic.

skills.name: Filipino Embroidery

Good lighting and a comfortable workspace

faqs.q: Is embroidery hard to learn?
faqs.a: Basic stitches are beginner-friendly. Consistency comes with short, regular practice.

faqs.q: Can I embroider on everyday clothes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask your mentor about fabric choice and stabilizers before starting on a garment you care about.

skills.name: Parol & Lantern Making

Basic craft tools and a safe workspace
questions: What materials should I use for a first parol?

faqs.q: Can I make a parol without capiz?
faqs.a: Yes. Many beginners use paper, plastic, or other translucent materials. Ask your mentor what is locally available and safe.

faqs.q: How long does a first parol take?
faqs.a: A simple parol can take a few sessions. Frame construction and drying time are usually the slow parts.

Finishing and caring for woven pieces

faqs.q: Can I learn Inabel weaving through PalTuro?
faqs.a: Yes. Inabel is a topic inside Philippine Handweaving. A mentor can teach the loom, patterns, and the tradition behind the textile.

faqs.q: Do I need my own loom?
faqs.a: Not always. Ask your mentor about shared looms, community workshops, or small-frame practice before buying equipment.

categories.name: Visual Arts & Design
categories.blurb: Painting and visual practice taught through observation, color, and guided making.
intro: Visual arts are learned by making, looking, and revising. A skills exchange gives you a mentor who can respond to your work and help you see what to practice next.
You can start with a small study, a color exercise, or a finished piece. The goal is a practice you can continue on your own.

faqs.q: Do I need to be good at drawing to start painting?
faqs.a: No. Many painting mentors start with color, shape, and simple studies. Drawing can be learned alongside painting.

faqs.q: What materials should I buy first?
faqs.a: Ask your mentor before buying a full set. A small set of paints, a few surfaces, and basic brushes are usually enough to start.

faqs.q: Can I learn painting online?
faqs.a: Yes. A mentor can demonstrate techniques on camera and review photos of your work.

skills.name: Painting
skills.summary: Learn color, composition, and brushwork through guided studies and feedback.
prepare: A small set of paints and surfaces
A reference image or object to paint
questions: What should I paint first?
How do I know when a painting is finished?

faqs.q: What paint should a beginner use?
faqs.a: Acrylic is forgiving and easy to clean; watercolor is portable and good for studies; oil takes longer but rewards patience. Ask your mentor what they teach.

faqs.q: How often should I practice?
faqs.a: Short, regular studies are more useful than occasional long sessions. Your mentor can suggest a weekly exercise.
